long_biography.plain_text:
Geoffrey Wilding kept Pacific Print Group’s business plan on one side of an A3 sheet. As its executive chairman, he assembled profitable printing companies while leaving technical decisions to experienced managers. At Vega Press, the acquired business retained its leadership and day-to-day purchasing decisions.

Wilding focused on the money tied up inside those businesses. He examined working capital, investment in machinery and borrowing levels, seeking to make balance sheets more efficient. When suitable New Zealand acquisitions became scarce, he chose to expand into Australia while retaining his requirements for financial performance and purchase price.
